transcript:
Meeting: Zenith Labs / Redwood Co-sell: Opportunity Acceleration & Handoff
Date: 2026-07-02T16:00:00Z
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Marisol Vega (Redwood Partnerships); Priya Anand (Zenith Head of AI), Daniel Ortega (Zenith VP Sales), Nora Li (Zenith CTO), Samir Patel (Zenith Procurement)

Summary:
- Quick pipeline scrub of the three prioritized Zenith opportunities (Pilot, Enterprise Renewal, Strategic POC).
- Align roles for co-sell outreach and exec intro; confirm pilot success metrics and legal path.
- Agree next steps: compensation spreadsheet, bench marking, enablement materials, procurement kickoff.

Topics:
- Pilot scope + success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds)
- Co-sell economics and lead routing (referral vs. joint motion)
- Procurement and legal checklist (SLA, SOC2, data residency)
- Quick tech risk review: private deployment vs hosted, KV cache / prefix caching concerns

Action items (recap): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: All right, hey everyone thanks for carving time, uh Alex Kim from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this motion. Quick round of intros?
00:08 Priya Anand: Hi, Priya Anand, Head of AI at Zenith. We're excited to move faster on the pilot.
00:11 Daniel Ortega: Daniel, VP Sales. I'll be owning the commercial side with Priya.
00:14 Liam Chen: Liam Chen, technical lead from Redwood, I'll do the bench and the onboarding.
00:18 Nora Li: Nora, CTO. I'll jump in on the infra questions.
00:21 Samir Patel: Samir, procurement. I'll track legal and procurement timelines.
00:25 Marisol Vega: Marisol, Partnerships at Redwood, coordinating the co-sell motion.
00:28 Alex Kim: Cool. Goal today is two fold: one, unblock the pilot run and two, align on co-sell play and who does what. We have three deals in the Zen pipeline that we want to accelerate, I'm going to list them quick.
00:44 Alex Kim: Opportunity A is the evaluation pilot for their internal support automation, Opportunity B is a renew/expand with their analytics team, and Opportunity C is a strategic, cross-sell into their platform team. We're prioritizing A and C for joint motion.
01:02 Priya Anand: For the pilot (A) success metrics: 90th pct latency under 450ms for median prompt size, F1 on intent extraction above 0.88, and reduction in handle time by at least 20% in the first 60 days.
01:18 Liam Chen: Okay, that latency target—just to flag—depends on model choice and whether we run hosted or dedicated. If you need sub-500 consistently we should plan for Dedicated or a pinned lower-latency variant. If you go hosted with autoscale you might see more variance.
01:34 Nora Li: Can you say more about dedicated vs hosted? We have concerns about data residency and audit logs so private would be preferred if KL things get weird.
01:41 Alex Kim: Right, good question. For Zenith's regulatory case, private deployment (VPC) is an option. It adds a procurement step and lead time — typically 4–6 weeks for infra and networking, plus legal reviews. Hosted is faster to start but has some constraints on data residency we should confirm.
01:58 Daniel Ortega: On the commercial side, Daniel here: what's co-sell economics look like? Do we do referral fee or joint logo credit? Also how do we handle incoming leads to Zenith vs Redwood-originated leads?
02:11 Marisol Vega: We usually run a joint motion with a referral split for inbound partner-sourced deals and a revenue share on generated pipeline. I'll share the co-sell compensation spreadsheet after this call. We can do either referral or joint-branded plays—depends on the deal and the exec sponsor.
02:27 Priya Anand: We prefer joint credit for strategic accounts, referral for smaller ones. Also we need clarity on who handles contract negotiation.
02:34 Alex Kim: Typically Redwood owns the SaaS contract; Zenith gets partner credits and sales support. For on-prem or private infra, there's a different SOW structure — legal will need to review.
02:44 Samir Patel: Procurement question: what does the SSO / SAML integration look like? Also we need a SOC2 attestation and KMS integration options documented early.
02:55 Liam Chen: We support SAML and SSO; Redwood can integrate with your IdP for pilot. SOC2 reports are available — we'll share our SOC2 and ISO docs. For KMS, we can do customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments.
03:12 Nora Li: For the pilot, what's the minimal network topology? We want a simple path — not a huge infra project.
03:18 Liam Chen: For a quick start, hosted with VPC peering works; for stricter data residency we'll provision a VPC connector and a private control plane. We'll put together a diagram.
03:28 Alex Kim: Ok let's talk timelines: Priya, you said you want the pilot live in July — is that realistic?
03:35 Priya Anand: We want a 30–45 day pilot start ideally starting mid-July. So we need bench results and a quick enablement session week of the 12th.
03:42 Alex Kim: Good. Liam, can you run a perf pass on 5 representative prompts and share numbers by next Thursday?
03:47 Liam Chen: Yep, I'll run constrained bench on a medium GPU profile and a compact quantized model, share raw numbers + caveats. Target deliverable by 2026-07-08.
03:58 Daniel Ortega: What about competitive threats — we heard from the buyer that Anthropic and Cohere are in the mix. How do we position versus them?
04:06 Marisol Vega: We emphasize production economics, predictable latency and observability. We also lean on the unified API across hosted/dedicated/private which helps their SRE team avoid rework. I'll draft a short battlecard.
04:20 Priya Anand: Also can you show benchmarking on our specific prompts? Generic numbers don't fly with my team.
04:25 Liam Chen: Agreed — that's why I asked for sample prompts and a small dataset. Priya, if you share the sample by Tuesday, I can include it in the bench.
04:33 Priya Anand: I'll upload a sanitized sample to the shared drive.
04:36 Alex Kim: Legal path — Samir, what's your procurement window?
04:39 Samir Patel: For standard SaaS, 4–6 weeks after we finalize terms. For private on-prem or dedicated hosting with network work, add 3–4 weeks. We need SSO, SOC2, and indemnity language to move faster.
04:51 Alex Kim: We'll shoot the SOC2 and a sample SOW. Also we'll put together a minimal SAML integration doc.
04:56 Nora Li: One more tech risk — prefix caching and KV cache semantics. For our use-case caching may leak PII if not configured right. How does Redwood handle token-level caching and TTLs?
05:08 Liam Chen: Good call. We have prefix/KV cache controls and per-customer cache separation; TTLs are configurable and can be disabled for sensitive flows. I'll add notes to the tech runbook.
05:18 Priya Anand: Perfect. For success criteria we'll centralize on: latency, quality (intent F1), and cost per 1k tokens.
05:27 Alex Kim: Great. On co-sell ops — I propose: Marisol runs partner enablement and lead routing, Alex drives Redwood sales touches, Daniel drives Zenith internal champions. We set weekly syncs for the first 30 days. Any objections?
05:40 Daniel Ortega: Sounds good. Weekly cadence ok.
05:42 Marisol Vega: I'll send the calendar invite and enablement deck.
05:45 Alex Kim: Quick note on reporting — Redwood Console will provide per-route latency and token cost so we can jointly monitor pilot economics. We'll set a dashboard access for Priya's team.
05:56 Priya Anand: We want read-only and a weekly export for our execs.
05:59 Liam Chen: We'll set read-only console role and schedule exports.
06:03 Alex Kim: Okay let's do a quick risk heatmap now — call out top three risks and mitigations. Priya?
06:10 Priya Anand: Risk one: privacy / PII leakage with caching — mitigation: disable KV/prefix cache and use customer KMS.
06:18 Nora Li: Risk two: latency spikes on hosted autoscale — mitigation: dedicate capacity or model pinning for pilot.
06:25 Samir Patel: Risk three: procurement delay — mitigation: get legal contacts now and start SOW template swap.
06:33 Alex Kim: Perfect. Anything else that would block kickoff?
06:36 Priya Anand: Need the bench numbers and the enablement deck.
06:40 Alex Kim: We'll prioritize those.
06:43 Daniel Ortega: On co-sell credit and reference use — can we define a simple one-pager that both legal teams can sign? That will help us reference them publicly.
06:52 Marisol Vega: Yes we'll draft a short MOU and a reference-use clause in the MOU.
06:57 Alex Kim: All right final recap of next steps: Redwood to share compensation spreadsheet and co-sell MOU draft, SE to run bench on sample prompts, Partnerships to send enablement and portal access, Zenith to provide data sample and start procurement intake. Weekly sync invite from Marisol. Exec intro to be scheduled for week of 2026-07-12.
07:22 Priya Anand: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to it.
07:24 Alex Kim: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links.
07:28 [call ends]

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Co-sell compensation & GTM spreadsheet (link shared in chat)
